title: Build a budget that works, and bends in hard months

say: Build a budget that works, and bends in hard months.
This is the video for Module 3, Budgeting: Planning Your Money Month by Month.
A budget is a plan for your money, made before you spend it. This much is coming in, and this is exactly where it will go.

panel.heading: Tell your money what to do
items: A budget is a plan made before you spend
Tracking looks back; a budget looks forward

say: Tracking looks back at what happened. A budget looks forward. Together they form a loop: plan, spend, track, compare, improve.

panel.heading: Tell your money what to do
items: A budget is a plan made before you spend
Tracking looks back; a budget looks forward

say: A budget is not a punishment or a sign that you are poor. It means you decide in advance, calmly, instead of at the market or when a relative calls.

panel.heading: Tell your money what to do
items: A budget is a plan made before you spend
Tracking looks back; a budget looks forward

say: A popular guideline is 50 percent for needs, 30 percent for wants, and 20 percent for savings.
For example, Zainab, a nurse in Abuja, takes home about 250,000 naira a month. The classic split gives needs 125,000, wants 75,000 and savings 50,000.
But her real needs, including her mother's medicine, are about 175,000. That is 70 percent, and that is not failure.
So she cuts wants to 25,000 and keeps savings at 50,000. She protects her savings by trimming wants, not by pretending her needs are smaller.
Write your expected income at the top. Use take-home pay, or your safe figure if income is irregular. Then write savings first.

panel.heading: Fill your budget in this order
items: Giving, wants and a small buffer

say: Then fixed needs. Turn yearly costs like rent into a monthly line, so the money is waiting when the rent date comes.

panel.heading: Fill your budget in this order
items: Giving, wants and a small buffer

say: Then variable needs, using your tracking as a guide.

panel.heading: Fill your budget in this order
items: Giving, wants and a small buffer

say: Then a realistic giving line for church or mosque, family and events. Wants should be modest but not zero. And add a buffer of about 5 percent for things you forgot.

panel.heading: Fill your budget in this order
items: Giving, wants and a small buffer

say: If the total is more than income, cut wants first, then trim variable needs. If it still does not balance, income may need to rise.
Do not borrow for everyday needs. That only moves the problem to next month, with interest added.

panel.heading: Fill your budget in this order
items: Giving, wants and a small buffer
panel.rule: Never balance a budget by borrowing for everyday needs.

say: For example, Tolu and her husband in Lagos take home about 400,000 naira a month.
Savings go first: 30,000 for the emergency fund and 30,000 for school fees.
Their annual rent is about 1,200,000 naira. Divided by 12, that is 100,000 a month into a rent pot, plus 10,000 for the cooperative.
Food, transport, electricity, gas, data and toiletries come to 186,000. Food is the biggest line, so a weekly menu and bulk staples make a big difference.
Giving is 20,000, the buffer 10,000, and wants get 14,000.
It adds up to exactly 400,000 naira. Savings and rent are protected first, and wants get what is realistically left.
On payday, move savings, rent savings and school fees savings into their own pots first.

panel.heading: Payday and the weekly check
items: On payday, move savings and pots first
Divide food money into weekly amounts
Move money between lines, never from savings

say: Divide food and transport into weekly amounts. If food is 80,000 naira a month, give yourself about 20,000 each week. Overspending shows up in week one, while there is still time.

panel.heading: Payday and the weekly check
items: On payday, move savings and pots first
Divide food money into weekly amounts
Move money between lines, never from savings

say: Then spend 10 minutes each week writing actual spending next to the plan. For example, Ese in Benin City was 6,000 naira over on food. She moved 3,000 from transport and 3,000 from wants, and her savings stayed untouched.

panel.heading: Payday and the weekly check
items: On payday, move savings and pots first
Divide food money into weekly amounts
Move money between lines, never from savings

say: A good budget bends without breaking. Protect food, shelter and health first, then the costs that keep income coming. Cut wants first.
For example, Ngozi sells clothes in Onitsha. She usually plans on about 150,000 naira, but expects only 110,000 this month. She cuts wants, saving 12,000.

panel.heading: Ngozi closes a 40,000 naira gap
items: Food trimmed by bulk buying: saves 6,000

say: She reduces giving and explains to family that this is a tight month. That saves 7,000.

panel.heading: Ngozi closes a 40,000 naira gap
items: Food trimmed by bulk buying: saves 6,000

say: She cooks in bulk and buys staples with a neighbour, saving 6,000 on food.

panel.heading: Ngozi closes a 40,000 naira gap
items: Food trimmed by bulk buying: saves 6,000

say: She reduces her goal savings by 15,000, but keeps paying rent savings in full. Together that closes the 40,000 gap without borrowing.

panel.heading: Ngozi closes a 40,000 naira gap
items: Food trimmed by bulk buying: saves 6,000

say: Turn on transaction alerts. Never share your PIN, password, OTP or BVN with anyone, including someone who says they are from your bank.
Scams use urgent messages, sometimes from hacked accounts of friends. It is fine to say you will check your budget and reply in the evening. And avoid quick loans for everyday food and bills.

panel.heading: Stay safe when money is tight
items: Never share PIN, password, OTP or BVN
Urgency is not the same as emergency
Avoid quick loans for everyday bills
